name: Citizenship by Acquisition Through Marriage to a Tunisian Man

requirement_groups.name: Automatic acquisition (foreign wife whose own law strips her nationality on marriage)

requirements.blocker_text: A foreign woman marrying a Tunisian man acquires Tunisian nationality automatically (Article 13) if her own country's law causes her to lose her original nationality upon marrying a foreigner. No equivalent provision addresses a foreign man marrying a Tunisian woman.

requirement_groups.name: Declaration after 2 years' residence (foreign wife retaining her origin nationality)

requirements.blocker_text: A foreign woman married to a Tunisian man who retains her original nationality may acquire Tunisian nationality by declaration (Article 14) after the couple has resided in Tunisia together for at least 2 years.
requirements.fix_path: Reside in Tunisia with the Tunisian husband for 2 years, then submit a declaration.

evidence_required.document: Proof of origin-nationality loss (automatic track) or 2 years' joint residence (declaration track)

sources.title: ecoi.net (NGO-hosted country-of-origin information repository) -- French text of Tunisia's Code de la nationalité tunisienne, Articles 13-14: framed exclusively around 'la femme étrangère' (the foreign woman) married to a Tunisian citizen -- Article 13 automatic acquisition where her own law strips her original nationality on marriage; Article 14 optional acquisition by declaration after 2 years' joint residence in Tunisia where she retains her original nationality

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Tunisia). STATUS: DRAFT -- same sourcing limitation as tn_citizenship_by_descent.json. MARQUEE GENDERED FINDING, CONSISTENT WITH A PATTERN SEEN REPEATEDLY IN THIS DATASET (Qatar, Bahrain, Nigeria, Sudan, Somalia, Pakistan, Ghana): both Articles 13 and 14 are framed exclusively around the foreign WIFE of a Tunisian man; no equivalent provision addressing a foreign man married to a Tunisian woman was located in this build -- he would need to pursue ordinary naturalisation instead (tn_citizenship_naturalisation.json), with no marriage-based fast-track or exemption. GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE DUAL-TRACK STRUCTURE WITHIN THE GENDERED PROVISION ITSELF: unlike most countries' single gendered marriage-fast-track, Tunisia's law splits into two different mechanisms depending on whether the wife's OWN country's law happens to strip her of her original nationality upon marrying a foreigner -- if so, she gets automatic Tunisian nationality immediately; if her own law lets her keep her original nationality, she must instead wait 2 years and file a declaration. This makes the wife's path to Tunisian citizenship contingent on a THIRD country's nationality law, a structural dependency not seen in this exact form elsewhere in this dataset.
